content: Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium carbonate are available in various formulations, including extra-strength chewable tablets, extra-strength suspension, and regular-strength suspension. The recommended dosage for the chewable tablets is 2 to 4 tablets taken orally every 6 hours as needed, with a maximum of 16 tablets per day. For the extra-strength suspension, the dosage is 15 to 30 mL taken orally every 6 hours as needed, with a maximum of 80 mL per day. The regular-strength suspension can also be taken at 15 to 30 mL orally every 6 hours as needed, but the maximum daily dose is 120 mL. The safety and efficacy of these products have not been fully established. Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium carbonate can interact with several medications by altering their absorption or effectiveness. For example: 1. Raltegravir: These antacids decrease the drug's levels by enhancing gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents and is contraindicated, even with dose separation. 2. Atazanavir: These antacids reduce atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the drug's solubility. This interaction applies only to oral forms. It is recommended to avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, administer atazanavir 2 hours before or 1 hour after the antacid. 3. Baloxavir marboxil: These antacids reduce the drug's absorption by binding to cations in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Studies in animals have shown significantly reduced plasma levels when used with calcium, aluminum, or iron, but human studies are lacking. 4. Dolutegravir: These antacids reduce dolutegravir levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or administer dolutegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after the antacid. 5. Infigratinib: These antacids reduce infigratinib levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Avoid co-administration or administer infigratinib 2 hours before and after the antacid. 6. Misoprostol: Antacids reduce the bioavailability of misoprostol acid. Magnesium-containing antacids may worsen misoprostol-induced diarrhea. If an antacid is needed, use one containing aluminum or calcium. 7. Pazopanib: These antacids reduce pazopanib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use short-acting antacids instead of proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 antagonists, ensuring several hours of separation between doses. 8. Ponatinib: These antacids reduce ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Bictegravir: These antacids reduce bictegravir levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Administer bictegravir 2 hours before or after antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium. Routine simultaneous administration is not recommended. 10. Budesonide: These antacids reduce budesonide levels by increasing gastric pH, which may cause premature dissolution of extended-release tablets. Monitor therapy closely. 11. Cabotegravir: These antacids reduce cabotegravir levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after cabotegravir. 12. Dabrafenib: These antacids reduce dabrafenib levels by increasing gastric pH, which decreases its solubility and bioavailability. Use caution and monitor therapy. 13. Deferiprone: These antacids reduce deferiprone levels by binding to polyvalent cations. Separate administration by at least 4 hours. 14. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF: These antacids reduce drug levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. 15. Ethambutol: These antacids increase ethambutol levels by cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid administering aluminum-containing antacids for at least 4 hours after ethambutol. 16. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir: These antacids reduce drug levels by increasing gastric pH, which decreases ledipasvir solubility. Separate administration by 4 hours. 17. Nilotinib: These antacids reduce nilotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer antacids 2 hours before or after nilotinib. 18. Omadacycline: These antacids reduce omadacycline levels by impairing absorption due to cation binding. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from antacids. 19. Pexidartinib: These antacids reduce pexidartinib levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours before or after the antacid. 20. Rifampin: These antacids reduce rifampin absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. 21. Riociguat: These antacids reduce riociguat levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by at least 1 hour. 22. Sarecycline: These antacids reduce sarecycline levels by impairing absorption due to cation binding. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from antacids. 23. Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir: These antacids reduce drug levels by increasing gastric pH, which decreases velpatasvir solubility. Separate administration by at least 4 hours. 24. Vismodegib: These antacids reduce vismodegib levels by altering solubility and bioavailability. The effect on efficacy is unknown. Warnings and Precautions: Do not use for the treatment of peptic ulcers. Consult a healthcare provider if sodium or magnesium intake is restricted. Do not exceed the maximum dose for more than 14 days. In kidney disease, consult a healthcare provider before use, as reduced renal function may lead to aluminum or magnesium toxicity. Discontinue use and consult a healthcare provider if heartburn persists or if there is difficulty swallowing. Antacids may interact with certain prescription drugs by altering their absorption or bioavailability. Consult a healthcare provider before use. Pregnancy and Lactation: Pregnancy Category C: Use with caution as the effects on fetal development are not fully established. Lactation: It is unknown whether the drug is excreted in breast milk.
